sections.text:
Embodied world models predict the visual consequences of candidate actions before execution. However, existing action-conditioned world models often adopt uniformly weighted visual generation objectives that can be misaligned with embodied prediction needs.

Even with explicit motion conditioning, these objectives can underemphasize spatially sparse changes that are critical to interaction. We propose KineWorld, a transport-aware world-modeling framework that extends robot kinematics from motion conditioning to the spatial allocation of generative supervision.

Kinematic Transport Lifting (KTL) constructs renderer-derived, camera-aligned transport fields from commanded robot motion. Transport-Aware World Diffusion (TAWD) calibrates their motion support on the video-latent grid and reweights future-RGB flow matching through a normalized mixture of uniform and transport-focused distributions.

We train KineWorld using ALOHA-AgileX bimanual manipulation data from RoboTwin 2.0.KineWorld achieves an EWMScore-P of 68.95 in single-view evaluation and a TWB-Score of 54.82 in multi-view evaluation. These results support a shift from appearance fitting toward action-consequence modeling for embodied decision-making.

summary.en: The paper proposes KineWorld, an embodied world-modeling framework that uses robot kinematics to allocate generative supervision. Kinematic Transport Lifting constructs camera-aligned transport fields from commanded motion, while Transport-Aware World Diffusion calibrates motion support on the video-latent grid and reweights future-RGB flow matching with a mixture of uniform and transport-focused distributions. The model is trained on ALOHA-AgileX bimanual manipulation data from RoboTwin 2.0. The authors report single- and multi-view evaluation scores and argue that the results support modeling action consequences.

sections.text:
Anticipation of vessel trajectories is an essential task when navigating at sea. This applies to both human navigators and autonomous surface vessels. Trajectory forecasting enables sub-routines such as collision avoidance to assess the situation and react accordingly in time.

This paper investigates Transformer and Performer models for trajectory prediction of surface vessels in confined waters. Using widely available position data from the Automatic Identification System (AIS), candidate models are trained and evaluated.

Historical information on how other vessels have moved in the local area surrounding each agent is conveyed using positional heat maps. The heat maps are generated using Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) and encoded with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) before entering the Transformer models.

The models are trained with quantile loss to efficiently obtain a model-aware prediction interval, as this is crucial for timely collision avoidance.

The proposed model architectures are shown to greatly outperform previous work while the inclusion of local heat maps enables the prediction of vessel movement that is not otherwise indicated from the previous positions.

summary.en: The paper studies Transformer and Performer models for forecasting vessel trajectories in confined waters, training and evaluating them with Automatic Identification System position data. To represent nearby vessels’ historical movements, the authors create positional heat maps using Kernel Density Estimation and encode them with a Convolutional Neural Network before input to the Transformer models. Quantile loss is used to obtain prediction intervals for collision avoidance. The authors report that their architectures outperform previous work and that local heat maps enable predictions not indicated by prior positions alone.
summary.zh: 论文研究 Transformer 和 Performer 模型在受限水域中的船舶轨迹预测，使用自动识别系统（AIS）位置数据训练和评估模型。为表示各船舶周边局部区域内其他船只的历史运动，作者通过核密度估计生成位置热图，并用卷积神经网络编码后输入 Transformer。模型采用分位数损失，以获取适用于碰撞规避的预测区间。作者称所提架构显著优于既有研究，并报告加入局部热图可预测仅凭历史位置无法指示的船舶运动。

sections.text:
End-to-end planning in complex scenes must model diverse driving intentions and select the most appropriate trajectory using scene context and future risks.

However, multi-query regression may collapse to one mode, while anchor-based and generative planners share a scaling bottleneck: small candidate sets limit maneuver coverage or discovery of high-quality trajectories, whereas large sets increase generation and scoring costs.

We propose ManeuverFlow to generate trajectories for distinct intentions in one step and evaluate and refine them using current and future evidence. The model selects relevant maneuver modes, draws corresponding noise from the Gaussian mixture prior, and maps it to intention-specific trajectories through a maneuver-routed mixture-of-experts MeanFlow field.

Current features and future features predicted by the world model are aggregated along each candidate path into trajectory-specific evidence for PDM-factor prediction. Using the same evidence, the refiner predicts local Frenet residuals for selected candidates; refined and retained candidates are then jointly re-scored for selection.

With a lightweight TransFuser-style ResNet-34 backbone, ManeuverFlow achieves 90.6 PDMS and 90.1 EPDMS on NAVSIM v1/v2 navtest, respectively. On WorldEngine's recent 3DGS closed-loop benchmark, it attains the highest listed PDMS$^\ast$ scores of 75.19 and 74.58 under logged and IDM-controlled traffic, respectively.

Code: https://github.com/wyh-autonomy/maneuverflow.

summary.en: The paper presents ManeuverFlow for generating maneuver hypotheses and evaluating and refining trajectories in end-to-end autonomous driving. It selects relevant maneuver modes, samples noise from a Gaussian mixture prior, and maps it to intention-specific trajectories using a maneuver-routed mixture-of-experts MeanFlow field. Current features and world-model-predicted future features are aggregated along candidate paths for factor prediction and local Frenet-residual refinement, followed by joint re-scoring. The authors report NAVSIM v1/v2 navtest scores and the highest listed PDMS* scores on WorldEngine’s 3DGS closed-loop benchmark under two traffic settings.
summary.zh: 论文提出 ManeuverFlow，用于端到端自动驾驶中的机动假设生成、轨迹评估和细化。模型选择相关机动模式，从高斯混合先验采样噪声，并通过机动路由的专家混合 MeanFlow 场生成意图特定轨迹。它沿候选路径汇集当前特征及世界模型预测的未来特征，用于因子预测和局部 Frenet 残差细化，随后共同重评分。作者报告了 NAVSIM v1/v2 navtest 的 PDMS 与 EPDMS，以及 WorldEngine 3DGS 闭环基准在两种交通设置下的最高所列 PDMS* 分数。

items.title: ManeuverFlow: Maneuver Hypothesis Generation with Future Evidence for Trajectory Evaluation and Refinement in End-to-End Autonomous Driving

sections.text:
Safety-critical control of uncertain, adaptive systems often relies on conservative, worst-case uncertainty bounds that limit closed-loop performance.

Online conformal prediction is a powerful data-driven method for quantifying uncertainty when truth values of predicted outputs are revealed online; however, for systems that adapt the dynamics without measurements of the state derivatives, standard online conformal prediction is insufficient to quantify the model uncertainty.

We propose Staggered Integral Online Conformal Prediction (SI-OCP), an algorithm utilizing an integral score function to quantify the lumped effect of disturbance and learning error.

This approach provides long-run coverage guarantees, resulting in long-run safety when synthesized with safety-critical controllers, including robust tube model predictive control.

Finally, we validate the proposed approach through a numerical simulation of an all-layer deep neural network (DNN) adaptive quadcopter using robust tube (MPC), highlighting the applicability of our method to complex learning parameterizations and control strategies.

summary.en: The paper proposes Staggered Integral Online Conformal Prediction (SI-OCP) for systems whose dynamics adapt without measurements of state derivatives. The algorithm uses an integral score function to quantify the combined effect of disturbance and learning error and provides long-run coverage guarantees. The authors state that combining it with safety-critical controllers, including robust tube model predictive control, yields long-run safety. They validate the approach through a numerical simulation of an all-layer deep neural network adaptive quadcopter using robust tube MPC, highlighting applicability to complex learning parameterizations and control strategies.
summary.zh: 论文针对缺少状态导数测量、且动力学会自适应变化的系统，提出交错积分在线共形预测算法 SI-OCP。该方法使用积分评分函数量化扰动与学习误差的合并影响，并提供长期覆盖保证；作者指出，将其与鲁棒管状模型预测控制等安全关键控制器结合，可实现长期安全。论文通过数值仿真验证该方法，仿真对象为采用鲁棒管状 MPC 的全层深度神经网络自适应四旋翼，并讨论其对复杂学习参数化和控制策略的适用性。

items.title: Staggered Integral Online Conformal Prediction for Safe Dynamics Adaptation with Multi-Step Coverage Guarantees

sections.text:
Autonomous navigation in cluttered and constrained environments typically assumes a fixed environment and searches only for paths within existing free space. However, a route can be blocked by an articulated structure, a movable object, or a pedestrian, and reaching the goal may therefore require appropriate embodied interaction with the environment.

This paper formulates Path-Creative Navigation (PCN), a navigation paradigm in which the robot recovers free space by coordinating locomotion and embodied interaction, and addresses one class of PCN tasks with a mapless framework.

The vision-LiDAR-odometry framework integrates local observations, obstacle geometry, and robot-state estimates through a unified navigation system, providing stable semantic and geometric information for navigation and interaction.

The traversability-aware decision method utilizes visual and LiDAR distance information to determine whether a blockage is actionable and whether it can be safely bypassed, enabling the robot to interact only when necessary while supporting articulated structure pushing, movable object pushing, obstacle avoidance, and pedestrian requests.

We design simulation scenarios and evaluate different methods in both simulation and two real-world tasks that cannot be completed by conventional navigation alone without embodied interaction.

These results demonstrate that our framework achieves higher task completion than the baseline methods by coordinating navigation and interaction in cluttered and constrained environments.

summary.en: The paper introduces Path-Creative Navigation (PCN), in which robots recover traversable space through locomotion and interaction, and presents a mapless framework for one class of PCN tasks. The system combines vision, LiDAR odometry, obstacle geometry, and robot-state estimates, using visual and LiDAR distance information to assess whether blockages can be acted upon or safely bypassed. Evaluation in simulation and two real-world tasks reports higher task completion than baseline methods in constrained settings requiring embodied interaction.
summary.zh: 论文提出路径创造导航（PCN），让机器人通过移动和与环境互动来恢复可通行空间，并针对一类任务设计了无地图框架。系统融合视觉、激光雷达里程计、障碍物几何及机器人状态信息，并根据视觉与激光雷达距离判断障碍能否处理或安全绕行。仿真及两项真实世界任务评估显示，该框架在需要实体交互的受限场景中，任务完成率高于基线方法。

items.title: Towards Path-Creative Navigation: Robot Navigation through Embodied Interaction

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models and world action models (WAMs) have advanced robotic policy learning by building on pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) and video generative models (VGMs), respectively.

Yet VLAs learn without explicit supervision from future world states, while WAMs that condition actions on predicted futures incur extra inference cost and let visual prediction errors propagate into actions.

We present Forward Dynamics Models (FDM), a family of robotic action models that couples action and future world-state prediction through an action-to-future paradigm.

Future prediction is conditioned on action features, never the reverse: end-to-end training lets ground-truth future states supervise the policy through these features, while prediction errors cannot propagate into actions. At inference, FDM skips future generation entirely, avoiding its computational cost.

The paradigm is backbone-agnostic, and we instantiate it with both VLM and VGM backbones. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate the effectiveness of FDM across both backbone families, achieving a state-of-the-art 99.4% average success rate on LIBERO and absolute gains of up to 13% over VLA and WAM methods on real-world tasks.

summary.en: The paper presents Forward Dynamics Models (FDM), which predict future world states from action features and use future-state supervision to train the policy, while preventing prediction errors from propagating into actions. Future generation can be skipped at inference to avoid its computational cost. The approach is instantiated with vision-language and video-generative backbones. The authors report simulation and real-robot experiments, including a 99.4% average success rate on LIBERO and gains of up to 13 percentage points over VLA and WAM methods on real-world tasks.
summary.zh: 论文提出前向动力学模型（FDM），通过动作特征预测未来世界状态，并让未来状态监督策略训练，但不让预测误差传回动作。推理时可跳过未来状态生成，以避免额外计算；该方法可采用视觉语言模型或视频生成模型骨干。作者报告，仿真和真实机器人实验验证了两类骨干上的效果，并在 LIBERO 上取得 99.4% 的平均成功率，在真实任务中相较 VLA 和 WAM 方法最高提升 13 个百分点。

items.title: Forward Dynamics Models

sections.text:
Fast whole-body motion planning enables continuous replanning for humanoid robots in dynamic environments while satisfying collision avoidance and kinematic constraints. However, constrained motion planning incurs substantial computational cost due to repeated constraint projection in addition to collision checking and nearest-neighbor search.

Recently, GPU-based massively parallel planners have been proposed to reduce computational cost. Nevertheless, these planners still steer in the ambient configuration space, so projecting candidates that deviate from the manifold remains a significant source of overhead, particularly in highly constrained, high-dimensional problems.

In this work, we introduce PATACON, a GPU-parallel bidirectional planner that explores tangent space to exploit the local manifold geometry induced by known constraint functions.

Experiments on dual-arm closed-chain and humanoid whole-body constrained planning tasks show that PATACON outperforms the prior work as configuration-space dimension and constraint codimension grow, achieving up to an 11.25 times speedup.

These results suggest that GPU-parallel tangent-space exploration brings constrained whole-body motion planning closer to real-time performance.

summary.en: The paper introduces PATACON, a GPU-parallel bidirectional planner for constrained motion planning that explores tangent space to use local manifold geometry induced by known constraints. The authors identify projection of candidates that deviate from the manifold as a source of overhead in existing GPU planners that steer in ambient configuration space. Experiments on dual-arm closed-chain and humanoid whole-body planning tasks report that PATACON outperforms prior work as configuration dimension and constraint codimension grow, with speedups of up to 11.25 times.
summary.zh: 论文提出 PATACON，一种 GPU 并行双向规划器，通过探索由已知约束函数诱导的切空间，利用局部流形几何进行受约束运动规划。作者指出，现有 GPU 规划器仍在环境配置空间中转向，投影偏离流形的候选点会产生开销。双臂闭链和人形机器人全身规划任务的实验显示，随着配置空间维数和约束余维增加，PATACON 优于先前方法，最高加速 11.25 倍。

items.title: PATACON: GPU-Parallel Tangent-Bundle RRT-Connect for Constrained Motion Planning

sections.text:
We propose a safety-critical framework for the cooperative transportation of passive targets in microgravity, where a team of chaser robots acts through unilateral pushing contacts to track a human-provided desired twist while ensuring safe target motion.

The pushing-only nature of the interaction introduces sparse, configuration-dependent actuation constraints requiring chasers to physically relocate on the target body when the desired pushing allocation changes.

To address these challenges, we formulate a delay-aware feedback control architecture leveraging Control Lyapunov Function (CLF) and Control Barrier Function (CBF) constraints within a mixed-integer thrust allocation program to enforce stability and safety of the target, respectively.

The proposed framework enables reference tracking while guaranteeing obstacle avoidance with a circular obstacle despite intermittent control authority, providing a foundation for human-supervised cooperative transportation of free-flyers in space environments. The proposed framework is validated through Gazebo simulations.

summary.en: The paper proposes a safety-critical framework for cooperative transportation of passive targets in microgravity. Chaser robots use unilateral pushing contacts to track a human-provided desired twist; configuration-dependent actuation constraints may require them to relocate on the target. The delay-aware feedback architecture combines Control Lyapunov Function and Control Barrier Function constraints in a mixed-integer thrust allocation program to address stability and safety. Gazebo simulations validate reference tracking and avoidance of a circular obstacle despite intermittent control authority.
summary.zh: 论文提出用于微重力环境中被动目标协同运输的安全关键框架，由多个追踪机器人通过单向推挤接触，跟踪人提供的目标运动指令。由于可用推力受配置限制，机器人需在目标表面重新定位。控制架构将考虑延迟的反馈控制与控制李雅普诺夫函数、控制障碍函数约束结合，并通过混合整数推力分配程序分别约束稳定性和安全性。Gazebo 仿真验证了参考跟踪及圆形障碍物规避。

sections.text:
Non-prehensile manipulation with mobile robots has primarily targeted placement in coarse goal regions. Precision placement has been studied with manipulators on benchmarks such as Push-T, where an omnidirectional end effector can readily re-approach an object from any side.

For a mobile robot, correcting the same placement errors may require wide repositioning maneuvers around the object. We formalize multi-object pushing with a mobile robot as a multi-target assignment problem at tight tolerances.

We propose a diffusion planner with a causal factorization: each robot denoising step is followed by an object step conditioned on the current clean robot estimate. This factorization allows us to sample multiple object outcomes for a single robot plan, capturing the multi-modality of pushing.

We also design a set of pushing-specific costs for mobile robots, used for both guidance and best-of-$N$ sampling at inference. On Push-T, our planner attains the highest success rate of the methods we compare, while having the lowest rate of implausible object motion.

Across three multi-box pushing environments resembling warehouse scenarios, it raises the fraction of boxes placed by $21.5$ percentage points over an unguided baseline, and replans $1.8\times$ faster than a planner that denoises the two trajectories together.

Lastly, we deploy the guided planner on a TurtleBot 3 Burger with object shapes absent from the training data, where it places $85.0\%$ of objects within tolerance against Diffusion Policy's $37.5\%$.

summary.en: The paper formulates precise multi-object pushing by a mobile robot as a tight-tolerance assignment problem. Its diffusion planner alternates robot and object denoising, conditioning each object step on the current clean robot estimate to represent multiple possible outcomes. Pushing-specific costs guide planning and inference-time selection. On Push-T, it reports the highest success rate and lowest implausible-motion rate among compared methods. In three warehouse-like environments, the placed-box fraction rises 21.5 percentage points over an unguided baseline, with replanning 1.8 times faster than joint denoising. A TurtleBot 3 Burger experiment reports 85.0% of unseen-shape objects placed within tolerance.
summary.zh: 本文将移动机器人非抓取推物的精确多物体放置建模为严格容差下的多目标分配问题，并提出扩散轨迹规划器：机器人与物体交替去噪，物体步骤依据当前机器人估计生成多个可能结果。针对推物设计的代价用于引导和推理时筛选。在 Push-T 上，该方法在所比较方法中成功率最高、非可信物体运动比例最低；三种模拟仓储环境中，放置箱体比例较无引导基线提高21.5个百分点，重规划速度为联合去噪规划器的1.8倍。TurtleBot 3 Burger 实验中，对训练未见形状的物体，85.0%在容差内。

sections.text:
Pre-trained robot policies, such as Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, provide a strong foundation for generalist robotic manipulation, but adapting them to new tasks with only a few demonstrations remains challenging.

Directly fine-tuning a pre-trained policy often achieves strong in-distribution performance, yet it can distort the representations learned during pre-training and weaken the model's generalization ability under out-of-distribution shifts. We propose Retrieval-Anchored Representation Alignment (RARA), a two-stage adaptation method, to address this issue.

First, RARA retrieves representation features from pretraining with similar task intent and motion, and aligns the policy's representations of the target demonstrations with the pre-trained representations of the retrieved demonstrations.

Second, RARA fine-tunes the policy on the target demonstrations while limiting how much its representations of the retrieved demonstrations change during fine-tuning. By reducing the representation mismatch before action learning and preserving pre-trained knowledge during adaptation, RARA limits unnecessary representation drift during fine-tuning.

Experiments with Diffusion Policy and GR00T on 13 tasks in RoboTwin, RoboCasa, and on a real robot show that RARA improves the average success of fine-tuning by 9.5 points in-distribution and 13.6 points out-of-distribution, and outperforms all compared baselines. Project page: https://shua-kang.github.io/RARA_robot/

summary.en: The paper proposes RARA, a two-stage method for fine-tuning pretrained robot policies from a small number of task demonstrations while limiting representation drift. It first retrieves pretrained representations with similar intent and motion, then aligns target-task representations to them. During fine-tuning, it also constrains changes to representations of the retrieved demonstrations. Experiments with Diffusion Policy and GR00T across 13 tasks in RoboTwin, RoboCasa, and on a real robot report average success gains of 9.5 points in-distribution and 13.6 points out-of-distribution over fine-tuning, outperforming all compared baselines.
summary.zh: 本文提出 RARA，一种面向机器人操作预训练策略的两阶段微调方法，旨在用少量演示适配新任务并减少表示漂移。第一阶段检索任务意图和动作相似的预训练表示，并对齐目标演示与检索演示的策略表示；第二阶段在目标演示上微调，同时限制检索演示表示的变化。作者在 Diffusion Policy、GR00T及RoboTwin、RoboCasa的13项任务和真实机器人实验中报告，RARA相较微调平均成功率在分布内提高9.5个百分点、分布外提高13.6个百分点，并优于所有比较基线。

Action-conditioned world models offer a promising foundation for generalist robotic intelligence by predicting the consequences of actions. However, existing robotic datasets provide limited coverage of the diverse interaction dynamics required for generalizable world modeling.

Large-scale egocentric human videos offer complementary interaction experience, yet the embodiment gap between human hands and robotic manipulators hinders effective cross-embodiment learning.

Meanwhile, the predominance of successful demonstrations leaves failure dynamics substantially underrepresented, limiting the ability of world models to anticipate unsuccessful executions. To address these limitations, we introduce HF-WM, an action-conditioned world model that combines Human interaction learning with Failure-aware post-training.

To bridge the embodiment gap, we develop a dual-branch framework that couples video generation with auxiliary pointflow prediction, using stabilized pointflow as a unified motion representation across human and robot interactions while suppressing egocentric camera motion.

To improve failure modeling, we further perform Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) post-training on perturbed actions derived from successful demonstrations, guided by action alignment and physical plausibility rewards, enabling the model to learn plausible failure dynamics without paired ground-truth videos.

Extensive experiments demonstrate that HF-WM achieves state-of-the-art performance in action-conditioned video generation and exhibits strong utility for policy evaluation in downstream robotic tasks.

summary.en: The paper introduces HF-WM, an action-conditioned world model combining human interaction learning with failure-aware post-training to address limited interaction diversity and underrepresented failures in robot data. Its dual-branch design pairs video generation with pointflow prediction, using stabilized pointflow to represent motion across human and robot interactions while suppressing egocentric camera motion. GRPO post-training on perturbed actions from successful demonstrations uses action-alignment and physical-plausibility rewards to model failures without paired ground-truth failure videos. The authors report state-of-the-art action-conditioned video generation and utility for downstream policy evaluation.
summary.zh: 本文提出 HF-WM，一种结合人类交互学习与失败感知后训练的动作条件世界模型，以补足机器人数据中交互多样性和失败动态不足。其双分支框架将视频生成与辅助点流预测结合，用稳定点流表示人类和机器人交互中的运动，并抑制第一人称相机运动。模型还通过成功演示扰动动作进行 GRPO 后训练，以动作对齐和物理合理性奖励学习失败动态，无需配对真实失败视频。作者称，大量实验显示其动作条件视频生成达到当时最佳表现，并可用于下游机器人任务的策略评估。

sections.text:
Humanoid household manipulation requires the arms to act while the body balances, steps and changes posture. We present BiGym 2.0, an adaptation of BiGym for the Unitree G1 across 20 household tasks using a unified whole-body controller for demonstration and evaluation.

The suite provides 60 native human virtual-reality demonstrations per task with synchronised multi-camera views and full-body execution records. We benchmark vision-language-action fine-tuning, imitation learning, demo-driven reinforcement learning, and cold-start coding agents given the interaction budget of online reinforcement learning.

With the same onboard views, proprioception and whole-body controller for every method, vision-language-action fine-tuning has the highest nine-task mean, and agent-developed programs outperform every demo-driven reinforcement learning baseline on this mean and lead on bimanual reaching.

Cross-workspace stacking remains open, $\pi_{0.5}$ stays low on pick-box, and multi-object transport is hard for imitation learning, demo-driven reinforcement learning and coding agents. All environments, human demonstrations, and evaluation traces are open-sourced at https://github.com/swirl-uk/BiGym2.

summary.en: BiGym 2.0 adapts a household manipulation benchmark to the Unitree G1, covering 20 tasks with a unified whole-body controller for demonstrations and evaluation. It supplies 60 native human virtual-reality demonstrations per task, including synchronized camera views and full-body records. The benchmark compares vision-language-action fine-tuning, imitation learning, demo-driven reinforcement learning, and cold-start coding agents under matched onboard views, proprioception, and control. Vision-language-action fine-tuning has the highest mean across nine tasks; agent-developed programs outperform all demo-driven reinforcement-learning baselines on that mean and lead in bimanual reaching. Cross-workspace stacking remains open.

sections.text:
Humanoid and service robots operating in clut- tered human environments may encounter motion planning problems that are infeasible when all surrounding objects are treated as fixed obstacles.

The Minimum Constraint Removal problem, which we refer to as MCR, addresses this situation by identifying the minimum number of constraints, such as movable objects, whose removal enables a collision-free path. However, computing an optimal MCR solution is NP-hard.

In this work, we propose a graph-based heuristic pipeline that combines bidirectional feasible-set generation with fixed- length searches over reduced MCR graphs. We further derive an extended feasible-set generator for instances in which the candidates produced by the first generator do not contain a complete optimal removal set.

Across six benchmarks, the evaluated pipeline matches the exact solution in three cases and, in the remaining cases, selects at most 31.25% more obstacles than the optimum, while being between 3.4 and 33.7 times faster than exact search.

In one of the benchmarks, involving a manipulation task amidst clutter, selecting two rather than seven obstructing objects reduces the combined MCR, inverse- kinematics, and motion planning time from 84.72 s to 30.59 s.

These results indicate that the proposed approach provides a practical compromise between computational efficiency and solution quality for motion planning among movable obstacles.

Action-chunking policies predict future controls but execute only a prefix before replanning. How should a fixed action-token budget be organized to support execution? We propose LeapBot-JAC, which allocates sparse future-control references and dense execution targets within one shared action expert.

Both chains are supervised by demonstrated controls and jointly denoised at aligned physical-time positions. Directed attention allows execution tokens to read reference tokens subject to the host's visibility constraints.

JAC adds neither action tokens nor parameters and retains the host's world-modeling process; both chains participate in inference, while only the execution chain drives the robot. On LIBERO, JAC reaches 98.3% success with FastWAM and LeapBot-WA, up from 97.0% and 97.3%.

On zero-shot LIBERO-Plus, their success rates improve from 53.5% to 70.4% and from 73.1% to 77.3%, respectively. RoboTwin and two real-world tasks provide additional deployment evaluations. Single-training-seed comparisons and FastWAM ablations support action-role organization as a practical design choice under a fixed action-token budget.

sections.text:
Enabling humanoid robots to perform agile and adaptive interactions has long been a core challenge in robotics. Current approaches are bottlenecked by either the scarcity of realistic interaction data or the need for meticulous, task-specific reward engineering, which limits their scalability.

To narrow this gap, we present HumanX, a unified framework that compiles human video into generalizable, real-world interaction skills for humanoids, without per-task design.

HumanX integrates two co-designed components: XGen, an anchor-centric data generation pipeline that yields physically plausible robot interaction data from monocular video and augments it to create a diverse, scalable training dataset; and XMimic, an interaction-prioritized learning framework to achieve generalizable interaction skills from seconds of demonstration.

Evaluated across five distinct domains--basketball, football, badminton, cargo pickup, and reactive fighting--HumanX successfully acquires 9 different skills and transfers them zero-shot to a physical Unitree G1 humanoid.

The learned capabilities include complex maneuvers such as pump-fake turnaround fadeaway jumpshots without any external perception, as well as interactive tasks like sustained human-robot passing sequences over 10 consecutive cycles--learned from a single video demonstration.

Our experiments show that HumanX achieves higher generalization success than prior methods, demonstrating a scalable pathway within a class of anchorable interactions for learning versatile, real-world robot interactive skills.

items.title: HumanX: Toward Agile and Generalizable Humanoid Interaction Skills from Human Videos

sections.text:
Humans effortlessly react to the world; they adeptly return a tennis shot, catch a falling cup, step aside from a passing cart, or pass a box tossed during truck unloading. These everyday actions require anticipating a moving target and reflexively responding with the whole body within about a second.

Such visual reactive whole-body control remains challenging for humanoids, which must （1） coordinate whole-body control, （2） react to object dynamics in real time, and （3） ground perception in egocentric vision.

We study catching thrown boxes as a representative task that demands all three capabilities; existing systems cover only part of it, relying on end-effectors, motion capture, or marked objects. We present Reflex, a three-stage framework that learns these capabilities stage by stage while connecting them through a compact representation of object dynamics.

First, a state-based policy learns whole-body catching with reinforcement learning. Second, the policy learns to infer the dynamics of a moving box from delayed and incomplete observations. Third, an egocentric RGB-D encoder learns to recover this dynamics representation directly from visual observations while keeping the whole-body controller fixed.

This decomposition provides each capability with a direct training signal and makes visual learning substantially more scalable. In simulation, Reflex achieves 85.7% catch success from egocentric RGB-D, compared with 87.9% when given privileged box observations.

Temporal visual history is critical: removing it reduces success by 35.6 and 39.8 points on centered and laterally offset throws. On a real Unitree G1, Reflex catches human-thrown boxes with 65% and 40% success at 2.5 and 5 m, reaching 76% and 59% of human catchers' success at the same distances.

items.title: Reflex: Visually Grounded Reactive Humanoid Control

sections.text:
Artificial intelligence is beginning to automate scientific discovery, yet physical robot-policy research still relies on scientists and engineers to interpret experimental failures and decide how controllers should be revised.

We present EndoRSI (Endoscopic Recursive Self-Improvement), a human-governed, self-improving robotic research system in which the embedded EndoForge coding agent iteratively develops and refines endoscopic robot policies using evidence from physical experiments. Physical execution remains isolated within a safety-constrained runtime under human authorisation.

In motorised endoscopy, validation evidence first caused the agent to reject an initial action representation, while subsequent physical experiments falsified an offline-supported insertion strategy by revealing hazardous closed-loop behaviour absent from the source data.

Failed physical rollouts were then incorporated into policy revision; insertion success subsequently increased from 2/21 in the first generation to 17/21 in the fourth. The frozen final policy retained competence across visual and hardware shifts and was the best performing autonomous policy across six independent ex-vivo porcine specimens.

These results show that physical robot interaction can serve as experimental evidence for agent-driven robot policy research.

items.title: EndoRSI: Physical-Evidence-Driven Recursive Improvement of Endoscopic Robot Policies

sections.text:
Generalist robot policies are trained with imitation learning and are bounded by the quality and coverage of their demonstrations. Reinforcement learning can improve and extend them, either by fine-tuning the policy weights or by training a small module to steer the input noise of a frozen generative policy.

When tasks arrive sequentially, both approaches suffer from catastrophic forgetting. Fine-tuning on a task degrades prior tasks, and steering only shifts forgetting to the shared steering module. We propose Dream to Remember (D2R), which continually steers a frozen generalist policy toward new tasks, while retaining its earlier skills.

As the steering module learns a new task, a frozen pretrained world model rehearses prior tasks through imagined rollouts, anchoring the module to its earlier behavior without a replay buffer or new data. When the world model is faithful enough, D2R learns the new task entirely in imagination.

Otherwise, it learns the task in the environment while using the world model only to rehearse prior tasks. On CALVIN, D2R improves eight tasks in sequence entirely in imagination, raising average success from 63.7% to 74.8%, while LoRA fine-tuning on the same sequence drops it to 11.7%.

With a frozen off-the-shelf generalist policy and world model, $\pi_0$ and A2World, D2R learns unseen LIBERO-90 tasks in the environment while keeping $\pi_0$'s performance on the LIBERO suites it was fine-tuned on, even though the world model is not accurate enough for policy optimization.

Finally, on a real Franka robot, D2R improves three tasks in sequence entirely in imagination while retaining the earlier improvements.

items.title: Dream to Remember: Continual Steering of Generalist Robot Policies with World Models

sections.text:
Depth sensors are widely deployed across robotic platforms, and advances in fast, high-fidelity depth simulation have enabled robotic policies trained on depth observations to achieve robust sim-to-real transfer for a wide range of tasks.

Despite this, representation learning for depth modality remains underexplored compared to RGB, where large-scale foundation models now define the state of the art. To address this gap, we present DeFM, a self-supervised foundation model trained entirely on depth images for robotic applications.

Using a DINO-style self-distillation objective on a curated dataset of 60M depth images, DeFM learns geometric and semantic representations that generalize to diverse environments, tasks, and sensors. To retain metric awareness across multiple scales, we introduce a novel input normalization strategy.

We further distill DeFM into compact models suitable for resource-constrained robotic systems. When evaluated on depth-based classification, segmentation, navigation, locomotion, and manipulation benchmarks, DeFM achieves state-of-the-art performance and demonstrates strong generalization from simulation to real-world environments.

We release all our pretrained models, which can be adopted off-the-shelf for depth-based robotic learning without task-specific fine-tuning. Webpage: https://de-fm.github.io/

summary.en: The paper introduces DeFM, a self-supervised foundation model trained entirely on depth images for robotics. It uses a DINO-style self-distillation objective to learn geometric and semantic representations, and proposes an input normalization strategy to retain metric awareness across scales. The authors also distill compact versions for resource-constrained systems. On depth-based classification, segmentation, navigation, locomotion, and manipulation benchmarks, they report state-of-the-art performance and generalization from simulation to real-world environments. They say the pretrained models can be used without task-specific fine-tuning.
summary.zh: 论文提出DeFM，一种完全使用深度图训练的自监督机器人基础模型。模型采用DINO式自蒸馏目标，在整理的深度图数据集上学习几何与语义表征，并提出输入归一化策略以保留多尺度度量信息。作者还将模型蒸馏为适用于资源受限系统的紧凑版本。在基于深度的分类、分割、导航、运动和操作基准测试中，作者报告其达到最先进表现，并能从仿真泛化到真实环境；预训练模型可直接用于深度机器人学习，无需针对任务微调。

items.title: DeFM: Learning Foundation Representations from Depth for Robotics

sections.text:
Visual world models predict the consequences of actions from images, but planning with them is typically done by optimizers such as CEM and MPPI. However, these optimizers stall on long-horizon tasks where progress requires motion the objective does not reward, such as moving around a block before pushing it.

This paper revisits kinodynamic sampling-based motion planning for world models, using the learned model as the propagator of a tree search in latent space.

Our key insight is that the sampling strategies devised for high-dimensional search in configuration space apply directly to the latent space of a world model, where they rapidly expand through intermediate states that myopic optimizers never sample.

We present two exploration strategies for the high-dimensional latent space, nearest-neighbor-guided RRT and projection-based KPIECE, with GPU-native batched expansion for efficient device utilization. We evaluate with an off-the-shelf DINO-WM on four simulated domains and a real-world block-pushing task.

Our approaches match or exceed the success rate of CEM and MPPI at up to 13.8x lower planning time in simulation, and improve the success rate by 20% on the real robot.

summary.en: The paper studies sampling-based kinodynamic planning with visual world models. It argues that optimizers such as CEM and MPPI may stall on long-horizon tasks when progress requires intermediate motions that the objective does not reward. The proposed approach uses a learned model to propagate tree search in latent space, with nearest-neighbor-guided RRT and projection-based KPIECE exploration, plus GPU-batched expansion. Evaluations with an off-the-shelf DINO-WM cover four simulated domains and a real block-pushing task. The authors report matching or exceeding optimizer success rates, up to 13.8 times lower simulation planning time, and a 20% real-robot success-rate improvement.
summary.zh: 论文研究在视觉世界模型中进行基于采样的运动学与动力学规划。作者指出，CEM和MPPI等优化器在长时域任务中可能停滞，因为完成任务有时需要先采取目标函数未奖励的中间动作。该方法将学习到的模型用作潜在空间树搜索的状态传播器，提出最近邻引导的RRT与基于投影的KPIECE探索策略，并使用GPU批量扩展。在四个仿真领域和真实方块推动任务上的评估显示，该方法成功率达到或超过CEM和MPPI，仿真规划时间最高降低13.8倍；真实机器人成功率提升20%。

sections.text:
World-action models (WAMs) predict a robot's actions together with the observations those actions will produce. However, the strongest models rely on video diffusion transformers that are far too computationally expensive for resource-constrained edge devices.

We present SmolWAM, a latent WAM that we derive from the 2B-parameter Cosmos Policy by keeping its pretrained trunk and rebuilding its inference interface: single-frame visual latents, cached text features that preserve the trunk's attention sinks, 12 of 28 transformer blocks, and 1,008 tokens from which actions and future visual latents are read out in one rectified-flow step.

Trained in 3.6 GPU-hours, SmolWAM succeeds in 95.5% of 400 LIBERO episodes at 57 ms and 2.3 TFLOP per 16-action chunk with 2.4 GiB of GPU memory, 11x faster than its teacher with 18.5x fewer FLOPs and 3.2x less memory, and its world head still forecasts scene motion.

summary.en: The paper presents SmolWAM, a latent world-action model for robotic manipulation on edge devices, designed to reduce the computational cost of video diffusion models. It retains the pretrained Cosmos Policy trunk while rebuilding the inference interface, using single-frame visual latents, cached text features, a subset of transformer blocks, and one rectified-flow step to produce actions and future visual latents. Training took 3.6 GPU-hours. On 400 LIBERO episodes, it achieved 95.5% success, with 57 ms per 16-action chunk and 2.4 GiB of GPU memory; the authors report lower latency, FLOPs, and memory use than its teacher, while retaining scene-motion forecasts.
summary.zh: 论文提出SmolWAM，一种面向边缘设备机器人操作的潜在世界动作模型，旨在降低视频扩散模型的计算开销。它基于预训练的Cosmos Policy主干重建推理接口，使用单帧视觉潜变量、缓存文本特征、部分变换器模块及单步整流流读取动作和未来视觉潜变量。模型训练耗时3.6 GPU小时。在LIBERO的400个回合中成功率为95.5%，每个16动作块推理耗时57毫秒，使用2.4 GiB显存；相较教师模型，速度更快、计算量和显存占用更低，世界预测头仍能预测场景运动。

sections.text:
Translating language into humanoid motion requires coordinating body parts, determining motion duration, and producing references suitable for robot execution. We introduce PartiGen, a part-aware latent diffusion framework that incorporates anatomical structure into a shared whole-body motion representation.

Part-specific attention processes anatomically masked frame features, and its outputs are fused to combine local limb information with whole-body context. Conditioned on text and motion history, the model generates motion primitives autoregressively.

Forward-kinematics supervision encourages kinematic consistency, while a learned end-of-sequence predictor selects a frame-level endpoint after generation. On HumanML3D retargeted to the Unitree G1, PartiGen achieves a segment-level FID of 3.165, a 16.8% reduction over TextOp, and improves R@1 by 1.4 percentage points.

In the duration study with 16-frame primitives, endpoint prediction reduces mean absolute duration error from 12.471 to 3.080 frames compared with a fixed-length cutoff. We further evaluate robot execution using a pretrained, frozen GRIT tracker: 409 of 500 generated references (81.8%) pass the posture-based stability screen in MuJoCo.

Following simulation screening and manual selection, 26 of 27 attempted motions are judged successful on the real G1.

summary.en: The paper presents PartiGen, a part-aware latent diffusion framework that combines anatomically masked limb features with whole-body context to generate motion primitives autoregressively. It uses forward-kinematics supervision and predicts a frame-level endpoint. On HumanML3D retargeted to Unitree G1, the authors report better segment-level FID and R@1 than TextOp. Endpoint prediction also reduces duration error relative to a fixed cutoff. In MuJoCo, 409 of 500 references pass a posture-based stability screen; after simulation screening and manual selection, 26 of 27 attempted motions are judged successful on the real G1.
summary.zh: 本文提出 PartiGen，一种利用人体解剖结构的潜在扩散框架，通过身体部位注意力融合局部肢体信息与全身上下文，并自回归生成动作片段。模型以正向运动学监督促进运动学一致性，并预测生成终点。在 HumanML3D 重定向到 Unitree G1 的评测中，作者报告其片段级 FID 和 R@1 优于 TextOp；时长研究中，终点预测比固定长度截断降低了平均绝对时长误差。MuJoCo 仿真筛查中，500 个参考动作有 409 个通过稳定性筛查；经仿真筛查和人工筛选后，真实 G1 上尝试的 27 个动作中有 26 个被判定成功。

sections.text:
Long-horizon manipulation requires robots to retain task-relevant history while revising conclusions no longer supported by physical evidence. Retaining observations alone does not specify which completed conditions should be withdrawn after a disturbance or which obligations require repair.

We introduce REMM, Revisable Embodied Memory for Manipulation, a supervisory memory layer for a frozen G0.5 vision-language-action executor. REMM separates an append-only evidence history from revisable task state and explicitly links derived relations and completed conditions to their supporting facts.

When accepted evidence changes a supporting fact, it withdraws dependent conclusions and schedules targeted recovery at verified skill boundaries without updating the executor.

Across 51 physical trials, including operator-assisted runs, REMM improves mean recorded task progress over the strongest baseline from 57% to 91% in intervention recovery and from 43% to 70% in sequence recall.

Complementary video diagnostics show improved grounding of retained history into the next instruction, including comparisons with $\pi_{0.5}$-compatible high-level planner adaptations. These results support revisable memory as a practical interface for continued manipulation without policy retraining. Project: https://revanthsenthil.github.io/remm/.

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models have advanced generalist robotic manipulation, yet real-world deployment reveals a fundamental challenge: robots are equipped with diverse and heterogeneous sensor configurations, auxiliary sensors can fail unexpectedly during operation, and different robot embodiments often lack certain sensors by design.

A unified policy that can exploit auxiliary perceptual inputs when available while remaining reliable under sensor absence, whether incidental or by design, is therefore essential for practical deployment.

However, existing VLA policies couple action generation to a fixed sensor set through shared dense computation, making them brittle when sensors are missing and limiting their ability to specialize across diverse tasks and long-horizon behaviors.

We propose CoRE-VLA, a scalable and robust VLA framework that formulates action generation as context-conditioned sparse computation. Sensor availability gates modality-specialized experts, enabling graceful degradation under missing sensors without retraining.

Task intent further routes action-side representations to task-relevant experts, improving specialization across diverse tasks and long-horizon subgoals. While the framework is designed to accommodate different auxiliary sensors, we focus on depth as a representative and practically important auxiliary modality in our experiments.

Experiments on LIBERO, RoboCasa GR1 Tabletop, and real-world dual-arm manipulation show that CoRE-VLA achieves strong results on long-horizon and multi-task benchmarks, and outperforms both a dense-action-generator ablation and a strong pretrained VLA baseline, including in zero-shot generalization to unseen scenarios.

Modality analysis shows that CoRE-VLA can exploit auxiliary depth when available while remaining robust when depth is unavailable during deployment.

summary.en: CoRE-VLA frames action generation as context-conditioned sparse computation. Sensor availability routes inputs to modality-specialized experts, allowing operation when sensors are absent without retraining, while task intent routes action representations to task-relevant experts. Experiments focus on depth as an auxiliary modality. On LIBERO, RoboCasa GR1 Tabletop, and real-world dual-arm manipulation, the authors report strong long-horizon and multitask results, outperforming a dense-action ablation and a pretrained VLA baseline, including on zero-shot unseen scenarios. Their modality analysis reports use of depth when available and robustness when it is unavailable.
summary.zh: 本文提出 CoRE-VLA，将动作生成建模为由上下文条件控制的稀疏计算：传感器可用性选择模态专家，使策略在缺少传感器时无需重新训练即可退化运行；任务意图则将动作表示路由到相关专家，以支持不同任务和长时程子目标的专门化。实验聚焦深度作为辅助模态。在 LIBERO、RoboCasa GR1 Tabletop 和真实双臂操作实验中，作者报告该方法在长时程与多任务基准上表现强劲，并优于稠密动作生成消融和预训练 VLA 基线，包括对未见场景的零样本泛化；深度分析显示有深度时可利用它，无深度时仍具鲁棒性。

items.title: CoRE-VLA: Towards Scalable and Robust Vision-Language-Action Modeling via Conditional Routing of Experts

sections.text:
We study when communication emerges between autonomous agents and what role an innate action selection architecture plays. Two e-puck robots, reconstructed in PyBullet from their Webots model and validated against it, must find a feeding zone that can only be detected when a robot passes over it.

Each robot can emit a one-bit signal whose direction is detected by the receiver. Control is provided by a GRU recurrent network with a residual path, either operating alone or as a channel within an Embedded Action Selection Architecture (EASA).Fitness measures only the time the robots spend over the food.

When the robots receive a compass pointing to the food, use of the signal disappears completely. Without a compass, in a small arena, three independent runs achieved similar performance using different strategies: a referential signal, a permanent beacon, or no use of the signal.

As the arena expands, the strategy based on a referential signal generalizes best. In contrast, evolving directly in the large arena does not increase the frequency of communication, but it does separate the strategies, and the referential signal clearly outperforms solitary searching. Within EASA, innate reflexes constrain the network and reduce performance.

As its priorities evolve, evolution consistently weakens those reflexes. The results suggest that communication emerges in proportion to the value of the information it transmits, and that an innate scaffolding designed for isolated agents can be an impediment in a social task.

summary.en: The study examines when communication emerges between autonomous agents and how an innate action-selection architecture affects it. In simulation, two e-puck robots search for a food zone detectable only when crossed, using an optional directional one-bit signal. The authors report that a compass pointing to food eliminates signaling. Without a compass, small-arena runs produce referential, beacon, or no-signal strategies. The referential strategy generalizes best as the arena expands, while innate reflexes in EASA constrain performance and are weakened through evolution.
summary.zh: 研究考察自主智能体间通信何时出现，以及内在动作选择架构的作用。仿真中的两台 e-puck 机器人需找到只能经过其上方才能探测到的食物区，并可发出方向可辨的一位信号。作者报告，有指向食物的指南针时信号使用消失；无指南针时，小场地的多次独立运行出现了指示性信号、常驻信标或不使用信号等策略。场地扩大后，指示性信号策略泛化较好；EASA 内的先天反射限制网络并降低表现，进化会削弱这些反射。

items.title: The value of information and the emergence of communication in evolved e-puck robots

sections.text:
Humanoid robots have many degrees of freedom and contact surfaces, yet most loco-manipulation research restricts manipulation to the hands and avoids other body contacts with the environment.

To extend manipulation beyond the hands, we present PanTact, a system that learns humanoid whole-body dexterity, the capability to manipulate with any suitable body surface, directly from robot-free human demonstrations. Our key idea is to use contact as manipulation-centric information that transfers across embodiments.

Contact locations and timing specify the interactions needed to accomplish a task, while the robot chooses how to coordinate its body to realize them within its own physical constraints.

Specifically, PanTact captures, learns, and executes whole-body contact via: 1) a wearable, robot-free data collection interface that augments egocentric vision and bimanual UMI grippers with whole-body modular contact patches to record body contact locations and states; 2) a visuomotor policy that mitigates the egocentric observation gap and predicts whole-body contact goals; and 3) contact-aware whole-body control formulations that realize active contact goals using suitable robot surfaces.

We deploy PanTact on a Unitree G1 humanoid without additional body contact sensors, demonstrating whole-body dexterity involving body support, pushing, sweeping, and load-sharing. Website: https://pantact.github.io

summary.en: PanTact is a system for teaching humanoid robots whole-body dexterity from human demonstrations collected without a robot. It treats contact locations and timing as manipulation information that can transfer across embodiments, while the robot coordinates its body within its own constraints. The system combines a wearable demonstration interface, a visuomotor policy that predicts whole-body contact goals, and contact-aware whole-body control. The authors deploy it on a Unitree G1 without additional body contact sensors and demonstrate support, pushing, sweeping, and load-sharing behaviors.
summary.zh: PanTact 系统旨在让人形机器人从无需机器人的人类示范中学习全身灵巧操作，使身体不同表面也能参与操纵。其方法将接触位置和时序作为跨具身传递的任务信息，再由机器人依据自身约束协调身体动作。系统包括可穿戴式数据采集界面、预测全身接触目标的视觉运动策略，以及实现主动接触目标的全身控制。作者在 Unitree G1 上进行部署，展示了身体支撑、推、扫和分担负载等操作，且未增加身体接触传感器。

items.title: PanTact: Teaching Whole-Body Dexterity with a Wearable Contact Interface

sections.text:
Vision-language-action models (VLAs) offer a promising route toward general-purpose robotics by transferring semantic knowledge from large-scale vision-language pretraining into language-conditioned control.

However, most VLA evaluations emphasize aggregate manipulation success under changes in objects, instructions, or environments, leaving unclear how reliably these policies ground spatial descriptions in the physical scenes where they act.

We therefore ask a sharper question: how reliably can current VLAs translate spatial descriptions into appropriate real-robot behavior?

To investigate this, we introduce Spa-Bench, a real-robot benchmark that evaluates spatial grounding across six tabletop tasks covering Object State, Relative Size, Referential Description, Relational Placement, Ordinal Position, and Counting.

Our primary evaluation compares in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) spatial configurations while retaining training support for the relevant objects, concepts, and actions, reducing object and motor unfamiliarity as alternative explanations for failure.

Four diagnostic conditions further probe physical execution, sensitivity to wording, object-task associations, and recognition that no action is required. We release 4,092 episodes collected on the SO-101 robot arm: 1,200 human-teleoperated demonstrations and 2,892 real-robot evaluation rollouts from five state-of-the-art VLA policies.

Across the three fully evaluated policies, success falls from 67.5-73.3% on ID spatial configurations to 40.7-52.0% on OOD spatial configurations, while matched direct instructions improve success by 28.3-40.0 percentage points. These results show that the evaluated VLAs can often execute the required manipulations but lack robust spatial grounding.

Project materials, including videos, code, and benchmark data, are available at https://justintiensmith.github.io/Spa-Bench/.

summary.en: Spa-Bench is a real-robot benchmark for testing whether vision-language-action models ground spatial descriptions in physical behavior. It covers six tabletop task categories and compares in-distribution with out-of-distribution spatial configurations while relevant objects, concepts, and actions remain represented in training. Additional diagnostic conditions probe execution, wording sensitivity, object-task associations, and recognition that no action is needed. The authors report lower success on out-of-distribution configurations for the three fully evaluated policies, with matched direct instructions substantially improving results.
summary.zh: Spa-Bench 是一个真实机器人基准，用于评估视觉语言动作模型能否把空间描述落实为适当行为。它涵盖六类桌面任务，并比较相关物体、概念和动作已有训练支持时，模型面对分布内与分布外空间配置的表现；另设诊断条件考察执行、措辞敏感度、物体与任务关联及无需行动的识别。基准包含 SO-101 机械臂采集的示范和评估轨迹。作者报告，三个完整评估模型在分布外配置上的成功率较低，直接指令能明显提升成功率。

items.title: Spa-Bench: A Real-Robot Benchmark for Spatial Grounding in Vision-Language-Action Models

sections.text:
Robots need to anticipate how their actions will change the world, since manipulation success hinges on the resulting contacts and object motions.

However, existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies that predict future observations from shared features leave the forecast decoupled from the actions the policy will actually execute, and impose no physical constraints on how the scene may evolve. We introduce ForeAct3D, a framework for policy-grounded future world modeling within VLA policies.

Learnable geometric queries decode depth, semantic segmentation, and camera pose from the policy representation into current and future semantic 3D scene states, and the future queries are conditioned on the policy-generated action chunk to ground the forecast in the planned interaction.

A physical-consistency closure relates the two states through background staticity and instance-level rigidity, and anchors the wrist-camera pose to end-effector kinematics. These objectives shape the shared representation used for action generation during training, and no future prediction is required at inference.

Without robot pretraining, ForeAct3D achieves 98.3% average success on LIBERO and an average task length of 3.73 on CALVIN, outperforming its base policy on every suite.

Ablations show that semantic 3D supervision, physical consistency, and action conditioning each improve manipulation performance, and that action conditioning substantially improves future object localization.

Real-world experiments on spatial placement, object insertion, and sequential manipulation further raise average success from 6.7% to 37.8% over the base policy. The project page and code are available at https://github.com/anthonytao80-crypto/ForeAct3D.

items.title: ForeAct3D: Policy-Grounded Future World Modeling for VLA Policies

Recently, soft robotic procedures are being developed aiming at achieving targeted minimally invasive operations or drug administration in specific locations in the human body.

Accordingly, specialized path-planning algorithms need to be investigated for the estimation of efficient paths that would protect the delicate tissue structures and simultaneously satisfy a set of requirements for the efficient navigation of the robot.

In this context, we propose an image-based 3D pathplanning algorithm, which is an extension of the A* algorithm, for the navigation of a soft-growing robot inside the spinal subarachnoid space (SSS).

The proposed algorithm is capable of estimating a safe pathway towards the goal location, while ensuring the establishment of anchor points that facilitate the efficient steering of the soft robot. The algorithm is evaluated using a highly detailed model of the SSS with respect to its capacity to satisfy the robot movement requirements and path efficiency.

items.title: Image-Based Path-Planning for Navigation of Soft-Growing Robots in the Spinal Sub-Arachnoid Space

People often learn how an unfamiliar object moves through a small exploratory push, using its response to guide their next motion. Inspired by this behavior, we study humanoids pushing carts whose mass and caster stiffness are initially unknown.

Our object-centric framework closes online estimation, flow-based planning, and whole-body control into a loop, creating a tension: replacing the plan whenever the belief shifts disrupts the maneuver under way, while keeping it strands the robot on a path its evidence has ruled out.

Belief-Overlap Partial Inversion (BOPI) scales revision to agreement, inverting the flow under the old belief only as far as the beliefs disagree before reconstructing under the new one.

Across 18 simulated goals it lowers pooled final position and yaw error by roughly 33% and 47% against fixed-depth replanning, and on hardware it translates and turns a non-holonomic cart.

summary.en: This paper studies humanoids pushing carts with initially unknown mass and caster stiffness. Its object-centric framework closes online estimation, flow-based planning, and whole-body control into a loop. Belief-Overlap Partial Inversion (BOPI) scales plan revision to disagreement between old and new beliefs by partially inverting the flow under the old belief before reconstructing it under the new one. Across 18 simulated goals, it reduces pooled final position and yaw errors by roughly 33% and 47% versus fixed-depth replanning. Hardware results show translation and turning of a non-holonomic cart.

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models increasingly incorporate intermediate reasoning to improve robotic manipulation, yet existing approaches primarily reason about observed states without explicitly anticipating future scene evolution.

Extending such reasoning to explicit future rollouts at every inference step, however, introduces substantial computational overhead. We propose IG-VLA, a VLA reasoning framework that enables models to imagine the future and internalize the gist.

Our Latent Spatiotemporal Reasoning learns to imagine task-relevant future scene evolution directly in visual representation space, guiding action prediction without costly pixel-level video generation.

To further reduce inference overhead, we introduce Scene Gist Memory, which internalizes reasoning-derived scene-behavior associations into a compact Scene Gist Token, preserving the benefits of future reasoning while bypassing explicit future imagination at inference.

Extensive experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and VLABench demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of IG-VLA. On the LIBERO-Plus Language suite, both the reasoning and gist policies outperform the strongest baseline by nearly 6% in success rate.

The gist policy also achieves up to 6.38x speedup over baselines, reducing inference latency from 1081ms to 169.5ms per action chunk on a single NVIDIA A6000 GPU. These results demonstrate that future spatiotemporal reasoning can be effectively internalized for efficient VLA deployment.

summary.en: The paper introduces IG-VLA, a vision-language-action reasoning framework that anticipates task-relevant future scene evolution in visual representation space to guide action prediction without pixel-level video generation. Scene Gist Memory compresses reasoning-derived scene-behavior associations into a token, avoiding explicit future imagination at inference. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and VLABench are reported. On the LIBERO-Plus Language suite, reasoning and gist policies each outperform the strongest baseline by nearly 6% in success rate. The gist policy reaches up to 6.38x speedup, with latency per action chunk falling from 1081ms to 169.5ms on one NVIDIA A6000 GPU.

sections.text:
Embodied coding agents construct robot policies from natural-language instructions by generating executable programs and refining them from execution feedback. This refinement assumes that execution feedback reveals whether the task succeeded and, after a failure, provides sufficient evidence to guide program revision.

Aerial manipulation violates this assumption in two ways. Payload constraints restrict onboard camera coverage and leave task-critical outcomes outside the robot's view (partial observability), while strong dynamic coupling and limited control margins make physical interactions fragile (limited interaction robustness) and leave failure causes unresolved.

Re-examining the same feedback cannot recover observations that were never collected or separate failure causes that the available evidence does not distinguish. To acquire this missing evidence, we introduce Active Feedback (AF), an active "View and Probe" framework.

When execution feedback leaves unresolved questions, the agent synthesizes a separate diagnostic program that runs in simulation to inspect unseen outcomes from informative viewpoints (View) or test hypotheses about failure causes through targeted physical interactions (Probe).

Across six simulated aerial manipulation tasks with 60 trials per condition, AF reduces false completion declarations from 25 to 5 and raises final task success from 31.7% to 75% compared with terminal feedback under the same coding-agent configuration and task-execution limit.

Using shared robot APIs, task programs refined with AF in simulation run on a physical aerial manipulator without task-program source-code modification and complete multi-stage manipulation tasks in the real world.

These results show that executable diagnosis fills gaps in execution feedback for embodied coding agents, improving both completion assessment and program refinement in aerial manipulation.

summary.en: The paper proposes Active Feedback (AF) to help embodied coding agents address missing evidence in aerial manipulation. Payload limits can hide task outcomes from onboard cameras, while fragile physical interactions can leave failure causes unclear. AF generates a separate diagnostic program that runs in simulation to inspect unseen outcomes from informative viewpoints or probe failure hypotheses through targeted interactions. Across six simulated tasks with 60 trials per condition, it reduces false completion declarations from 25 to 5 and raises final success from 31.7% to 75%, compared with terminal feedback under the same agent configuration and execution limit. The authors also report that programs refined with AF in simulation ran on a physical aerial manipulator without source-code changes and completed multi-stage tasks.
summary.zh: 论文提出主动反馈（AF）框架，帮助空中操作中的具身编码智能体弥补执行反馈缺失的证据。载荷限制可能遮挡任务结果，脆弱的物理交互也会使失败原因难以区分；AF因此生成独立诊断程序，在仿真中从有信息量的视角检查不可见结果，或通过定向物理交互探测失败原因。在六项仿真任务、每种条件60次试验中，相较相同编码智能体配置和任务执行限制下的终止反馈，误报完成次数从25降至5，最终任务成功率从31.7%升至75%。作者还报告，仿真中经AF改进的任务程序无需修改源代码即可在实体空中操作机器人上运行，并完成多阶段任务。

sections.text:
Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn compact latent world models without pixel reconstruction. Existing JEPA pipelines typically train visual representations and action-conditioned dynamics before adding a control policy or solver.

We introduce LeWAM, an end-to-end JEPA for control with: （1） a joint training objective over next latent state prediction and action flow matching, and （2） an isotropic Gaussian constraint on the latent state, enabling a single model to support direct policy execution and efficient planning by evaluating sampled actions with its learned latent dynamics.

Compared with prior JEPAs in visual planning, LeWAM improves success rate from 28.6% to 89.7% on contact-rich tasks and from 10.9% to 46.2% on long-horizon tasks, and plans 32.3 times faster. On behavior cloning tasks in simulation and physical robots, LeWAM is also competitive with established methods.

Interpretability analyses show that LeWAM learns control-relevant representations and action distributions effectively guiding test-time planning and control.

summary.en: The paper presents LeWAM, an end-to-end joint-embedding predictive architecture for control. It jointly trains next-latent-state prediction and action flow matching, with an isotropic Gaussian constraint on latent states. The model supports direct policy execution and planning by evaluating sampled actions with learned latent dynamics. Compared with prior JEPAs in visual planning, reported success rises from 28.6% to 89.7% on contact-rich tasks and from 10.9% to 46.2% on long-horizon tasks, while planning is 32.3 times faster. On behavior-cloning tasks in simulation and on physical robots, it is competitive with established methods. Interpretability analyses indicate control-relevant representations and action distributions that guide test-time planning and control.

sections.text:
Runtime failure monitors for robot policies are typically evaluated by how accurately they distinguish failed from successful executions. Yet an accurate alarm may arrive too late for recovery, while an unnecessary intervention may disrupt an execution that would otherwise succeed.

We introduce RESCUE, a counterfactual framework for evaluating whether a monitor's alarms enable useful interventions.

By restoring simulator and policy states at execution checkpoints, RESCUE compares alternative actions, identifies the latest checkpoint satisfying a specified recovery criterion, and evaluates whether acting on alarms reduces expected task-completion cost.

We evaluate RESCUE with OpenVLA-OFT and $\pi_{0.5}$ over LIBERO-Spatial and LIBERO-Plus using 128,340 counterfactual branches.

Recoverability depends on the state--intervention pair rather than on robot state alone: at $\tau=0.5$, 14 of 66 OpenVLA-OFT/LIBERO-Plus failures contain a recoverable checkpoint under continuation, compared with 34 of 66 under continuation or scripted recovery, while recovery reduces recoverability in other conditions.

On the primary strong-policy conditions, favourable detection scores do not establish lower intervention cost. Under the evaluated stop-and-reset model, even an idealised detector can afford only a 2.0--3.3% false-alarm rate before unnecessary resets outweigh the savings from stopping failures early.

These results show that monitor value depends jointly on the intervention available and the workload in which it is deployed.

summary.en: The paper introduces RESCUE, a counterfactual framework for assessing whether runtime monitor alarms support useful interventions for robot policies. It restores simulator and policy states at execution checkpoints, compares alternative actions, identifies the latest checkpoint meeting a recovery criterion, and evaluates effects on expected task-completion cost. Evaluations with specified models and benchmarks suggest recoverability depends on both state and intervention. In primary strong-policy conditions, favourable detection scores do not imply lower intervention cost; under the evaluated stop-and-reset model, excessive false alarms can outweigh savings from stopping failures early.
summary.zh: 论文提出 RESCUE，用反事实评估判断机器人策略运行时监视器发出的警报是否支持有效干预。该方法在执行检查点恢复仿真器和策略状态，比较替代动作，确定满足恢复标准的最晚检查点，并评估干预对预期任务完成成本的影响。作者在指定模型和基准上评估后指出，可恢复性取决于状态与干预的组合；在主要强策略条件下，较好的检测分数并不意味着干预成本更低。其停止并重置模型下，误报率过高会使不必要的重置抵消提前停止失败的收益。

sections.text:
Learning from Demonstrations (LfD) enables robots to learn object manipulation directly from human demonstrations. In contrast to resource-intensive and labor-intensive teleoperation, egocentric demonstrations are easy to collect, enabling scalable data collection.

Manipulated objects are often partially occluded in everyday environments, yet prior egocentric demonstration-based methods that require no robots or specialized teaching devices do not explicitly address occlusions.

To fill this gap, we propose EgoReveal, a framework that learns viewpoint-repositioning together with manipulation actions from egocentric human demonstrations to reposition the viewpoint and obtain target visibility under partial occlusions.

EgoReveal instantiates this as two imitation policies: one predicts the future camera-arm pose sequence from the current view and camera-arm pose, and the other predicts the future control commands from object keypoints and a history of control commands. EgoReveal switches between the two based on target visibility.

In experiments where the manipulated object is partially occluded initially, EgoReveal repositions the camera to obtain visibility and completes the task more reliably than fixed-camera baselines.

summary.en: The paper presents EgoReveal, a framework that learns viewpoint repositioning and object manipulation from egocentric human demonstrations to address partial occlusions. It uses two imitation policies: one predicts a future camera-arm pose sequence from the current view and pose, while the other predicts control commands from object keypoints and control history. The framework switches between them according to target visibility. In experiments with initially occluded objects, the authors report that EgoReveal moves the camera to reveal the target and completes tasks more reliably than fixed-camera baselines.
summary.zh: 论文提出 EgoReveal，利用第一人称人类演示学习视角调整与物体操作，以应对目标物体被部分遮挡的情况。框架包含两个模仿策略：一个根据当前视图和相机机械臂姿态预测未来姿态序列，另一个根据物体关键点及控制历史预测后续控制指令，并依据目标可见性在二者间切换。作者报告，在物体初始被部分遮挡的实验中，EgoReveal 会移动相机以获得目标视野，并比固定相机基线更可靠地完成任务。

sections.text:
Deploying generalist robotic agents in the real world requires transferable skills. Specifically, a policy trained to clone a behavior from object-specific demonstrations must generalize beyond that object, otherwise data collection requirements become intractable.

Recently, fine-tuning of pre-trained billion-parameter Vision-Language Models (VLMs), initially on large-scale robot datasets and then on fewer scenario-specific demonstrations, has emerged as the predominant paradigm for designing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models.

While these policies achieve state-of-the-art manipulation performance in-distribution, they remain brittle to minor spatial, semantic, and task variations.

In this work, we address the inability of current models to decouple the declarative (i.e., concepts and entity semantics) from the procedural knowledge (i.e., how to do something) encoded in their parameters, which is a fundamental bottleneck for zero-shot skill transfer to novel objects.

To address this, we propose w$^{2}$VLA, a new VLA model with restructured information flow. Rather than feeding all multimodal tokens from the VLM encoder into a large, opaque transformer-based action expert, our approach modulates the robot state sequence with visual, spatial, and skill information in a compositional and interpretable manner.

Unlike popular, state-of-the-art VLAs, we show that our modular approach successfully decouples knowledge representations, enabling robust behavior cloning and unprecedented zero-shot skill transfer capabilities across dissimilar, unseen objects.

summary.en: The paper proposes w²VLA to address the difficulty of separating declarative knowledge, such as concepts and entity semantics, from procedural knowledge in vision-language-action models. It restructures information flow: instead of sending all multimodal encoder tokens to a large action expert, it modulates robot state sequences compositionally using visual, spatial, and skill information. The authors claim this modular design decouples knowledge representations and enables robust behavior cloning and zero-shot skill transfer across dissimilar, unseen objects. The abstract does not specify the evaluation scope for these claims.
summary.zh: 论文针对视觉语言动作模型难以将概念与实体语义等陈述性知识，同操作方式等程序性知识分离的问题，提出 w²VLA。该模型重新组织信息流，不再将视觉语言模型编码器的全部多模态令牌输入大型动作专家，而是以组合且可解释的方式，用视觉、空间和技能信息调节机器人状态序列。作者称，该模块化方法实现了知识表征解耦，并在行为克隆和面向不同未见物体的零样本技能迁移方面展现出能力；摘要未说明这些结果所依据的具体实验范围。

items.title: Decoupling the Declarative from the Procedural in Vision-Language-Action Models

sections.text:
Robots must generate trajectories that remain faithful to learned expert behavior while satisfying safety constraints and task-specific objectives specified only at inference time.

We formulate constrained trajectory generation for pretrained diffusion and flow-matching policies as Bayesian posterior sampling, with the learned demonstration distribution as a prior and an inference-time, cost-derived likelihood tilting it toward feasible, optimal trajectories.

To sample from this posterior without any retraining of the base policy, we leverage the Feynman--Kac corrector framework, originally formulated for diffusion models, and extend it to deterministic flow-matching policies. The result is a unified, inference-time, retraining-free sampler for diffusion and flow policies.

We validate the approach on pretrained Diffusion Policy, GR00T-N1.6, and $\pi_{0.5}$ checkpoints across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, including planning around non-convex obstacles introduced at inference time, and show improvements over the base $\pi_{0.5}$ on zero-shot tasks.

summary.en: The paper formulates constrained trajectory generation for pretrained diffusion and flow-matching policies as Bayesian posterior sampling. The learned demonstration distribution serves as a prior, while an inference-time, cost-derived likelihood favours feasible and optimal trajectories. The authors use the Feynman–Kac corrector framework and extend it to deterministic flow-matching policies, yielding a sampler that requires no base-policy retraining. They evaluate pretrained checkpoints on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, including planning around non-convex obstacles introduced at inference time, and report improvements over the base π₀.₅ on zero-shot tasks.
summary.zh: 论文将预训练扩散策略和流匹配策略的约束轨迹生成表述为贝叶斯后验采样：以学习到的示范分布为先验，并用推理时由成本构造的似然引导采样趋向可行且较优的轨迹。作者借助费曼–卡茨校正框架，并将其扩展到确定性流匹配策略，形成无需重训练的推理时采样方法。论文在模拟和真实操作任务中评估了多个预训练检查点，包括推理时加入非凸障碍的规划；作者报告该方法在零样本任务上优于基础 π₀.₅。

items.title: BayesFP: Posterior Estimation for Flow-Based Policies via Feynman-Kac Sampling

sections.text:
Online policy learning directly in the physical world is a promising yet challenging direction for embodied intelligence. Unlike simulation, real-world systems cannot be arbitrarily accelerated, cheaply reset, or massively replicated, suggesting that real-world policy learning is not merely an algorithmic problem, but inherently a systems problem.

We present USER, a \underline{U}nified and extensible \underline{S}yst\underline{E}m for real-world online policy lea\underline{R}ning. On the systems side, USER introduces a hardware abstraction layer for unified robot management and an adaptive communication plane that enables efficient cloud-edge training.

On the learning side, USER adopts a fully asynchronous training framework, designs a persistent and cache-aware replay buffer, and provides extensible abstractions for rewards, algorithms, and policies.

Experiments in both simulation and the real world demonstrate that USER supports multi-robot coordination, heterogeneous manipulators, cloud-edge training with large models, and long-running asynchronous training. Together, these capabilities establish USER as a unified and extensible systems foundation for real-world online policy learning.

summary.en: The paper presents USER, a unified and extensible system for online policy learning in the physical world. Its systems components include a hardware abstraction layer for robot management and an adaptive communication plane for cloud-edge training. Its learning components include fully asynchronous training, a persistent cache-aware replay buffer, and extensible abstractions for rewards, algorithms, and policies. Simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate support for multi-robot coordination, heterogeneous manipulators, cloud-edge training with large models, and long-running asynchronous training.
summary.zh: 论文提出 USER，一个面向真实世界在线策略学习的统一、可扩展系统。系统侧包含用于统一机器人管理的硬件抽象层，以及支持云边高效训练的自适应通信平面；学习侧采用全异步训练框架、持久且考虑缓存的回放缓冲区，并提供奖励、算法和策略的扩展抽象。仿真与真实世界实验表明，该系统支持多机器人协同、异构操作臂、大模型云边训练及长时间异步训练。
